h: Daffodil dales and steam on the moors
p: Ryedale Folk Museum is at its loveliest when you tie it into the landscape around Hutton-le-Hole. In spring, nearby Farndale is famous for its wild daffodils, which carpet the banks of the River Dove for miles, and a walk along the dale is a real seasonal treat. Come in late summer and the heather turns the moors purple, while autumn brings golden bracken and crisp walking weather, so there's a good reason to visit at any time of year.

Lastingham, a short drive or walk away, is a tiny village with a remarkable church with an ancient Norman crypt, built on the site of an early Christian monastery. It's a peaceful, atmospheric place that sits beautifully alongside the stories told at the museum.

Back in Pickering, the North Yorkshire Moors Railway runs steam trains up through Newtondale to Goathland, which fans may recognise from TV, and on to Grosmont and, at times, all the way to Whitby. Pickering Castle, looked after by English Heritage, is a fine old fortress on the edge of town with views across the Vale of Pickering, and the town has plenty of tearooms and pubs for a well-earned sit-down.

At the museum itself, try to give the galleries and the outdoor buildings equal attention, as the indoor collections are rich and easy to skip in a rush. On event days, craft demonstrations and seasonal activities add a lot, so a quick check on what's coming up is worth doing. Sturdy shoes and a light waterproof will see you right, whatever the moors decide to throw at you.
